subject: Problem reproducing ggplot2 object with Shiny

messages.author: 58d4347d38332c5c
messages.subject: Problem reproducing ggplot2 object with Shiny
parts:
Hello shiny enthusiasts,

I am in the midst of writing an app to showcase my R package pitchRx (still in production). Here is an example of a plot (png attached) that I wish to reproduce with shiny:

library(devtools)
install_github('pitchRx', 'cpsievert')
library(pitchRx)
data(pitches, package='pitchRx')
strikeFX(pitches, geom="hex", density1=list(des="Called Strike"), layer=facet_grid(.~stand)) #Returns ggplot2 object I wish to reproduce (with shiny)

For some reason, when I use shiny to produce the same plot, I get a funny result. It seems as though the correct left-hand plot is produced, but is cut in half with the bottom half on the right-hand plot (png attached). If you would like to reproduce the error, use this: library(shiny); runGist(4440099). When prompted by your browser, scroll down to the "Plotting Geometries" section and choose "hex". Lastly, go to the "Alter Density(ies)" section and select "des" as the first variable of interest.

It's worth noting that this issue doesn't occur for a "classic" 2D density. It seems to only happen when strikeFX plots the difference of two different 2D density estimates.

Thanks in advance,

-Carson

Carson Sievert
Graduate Student

Iowa State University

messages.author: d34d025a513c07fc
messages.subject: Re: Problem reproducing ggplot2 object with Shiny
parts:
I haven't looked at how strikeFX is implemented, but it's possible that you're running into a bug in ggplot2's evaluation of aes(). By default, aes() is evaluated in the global environment, even when it should be evaluated in a different environment.

See
  https://groups.google.com/d/topic/shiny-discuss/s_c4QKAvquM/discussion
and 
  https://github.com/hadley/ggplot2/issues/743


(Side note: I'm unable to successfully run your gist - in the plotting area it says  Error: could not find function "theme")

-Winston

messages.author: d34d025a513c07fc
messages.subject: Re: Problem reproducing ggplot2 object with Shiny
parts:
Hm, the next thing I'd suggest is to remove things from your app until you have the absolute minimum that's necessary to reproduce the bug (this includes getting rid of ui stuff that's not needed).

For example, when I modify your output$plotFX function to just do the following, the output is as expected:
output$plotFX <- reactivePlot(function() {
  data(pitches, package='pitchRx')
  print(strikeFX(pitches, geom="hex", density1=list(des="Called Strike"), layer=facet_grid(.~stand)))
}

If you were to transition from that code to your current version, bit by bit, you'll find which change is causing the bad output. That will help to figure out if the problem has to do with shiny/ggplot2, or with your code.


Also, sorry about the false alarm about the ggplot2 theme issue -- it turns out the ggplot2 problem was because I was using an old development version of it.

Good luck!
-Winston

messages.subject: Re: Problem reproducing ggplot2 object with Shiny
parts: On Tue, Jan 8, 2013 at 12:45 PM, Carson Sievert <cpsie...@gmail.com> wrote:

Aha, I think I found the culprit. It has to do with my construction of the facet_layer object below:


output$plotFX <- reactivePlot(function() {
  data(pitches, package='pitchRx')
  print(strikeFX(pitches, geom="hex", density1=list(des="Called Strike"), layer=facet_layer))
}

In this case, I want facet_layer to pass along facet_grid(.~stand). If I want to construct this language from strings, it seems odd to me that:

> facet_layer <- facet_grid(".~stand")
> facet_layer
facet_grid( ~ stand)

Is there is a good reason why facet_grid does this?

The result looks the same for me whether or not I use quotes:
> facet_grid(. ~ stand)
facet_grid( ~ stand) 

> facet_grid(". ~ stand")
facet_grid( ~ stand) 

Also, both of these give me the same output:

strikeFX(pitches, geom="hex", density1=list(des="Called Strike"), layer=facet_grid(.~stand))
strikeFX(pitches, geom="hex", density1=list(des="Called Strike"), layer=facet_grid(".~stand"))
-Winston

messages.author: 58d4347d38332c5c
messages.subject: Re: Problem reproducing ggplot2 object with Shiny
parts:
Ugh. I finally fixed the issue. When I originally wrote strikeFX, I programmed assuming that the user would input facet_grid(...) directly into the layer parameter (instead of a call referencing variables from another environment). As a result, the density calculation within strikeFX was failing to recognize that facets were present, even though ggplot somehow picked that up. You can take a peak at what changed in strikeFX here.

Thanks for your help Winston!

-Carson
